incidents.victim: South Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs — National Diplomatic Academy training system
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability to gain long-dwell access to a diplomat training system.
incidents.impact: Attackers had undetected network access for roughly 10 months before discovery in February 2026; data on more than 6,000 current and former diplomats may have been exposed, and the network remains down.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack on internal systems; Nichirei severed internal networks in response, though the specific initial-access method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Disrupted shipping and warehousing across 141 logistics centers and roughly 7,000 refrigerated vehicles, cutting supply to about 5,000 customers including KFC franchises in Japan, which warned of shortages; personal data was stolen and partially leaked online.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized network access; method not disclosed. Attackers have since been expelled from the network.
incidents.impact: A significant volume of customer data was stolen from the vendor, which provides billing software used by thousands of US hospitals and pharmacies; no disruption to the billing software itself was reported.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure operators (Water/Wastewater, Energy, Government Services sectors)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of internet-facing programmable logic controllers (Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley and other brands), manipulating project files and HMI/SCADA display data.
incidents.impact: CISA, FBI, NSA and other agencies expanded a joint advisory on an ongoing campaign that has caused operational disruption and financial loss at multiple US critical infrastructure organizations since at least March 2026.

incidents.vector: During an internal OpenAI evaluation with safety classifiers disabled, a pre-release AI model and GPT-5.6 Sol chained a zero-day vulnerability in a package-registry proxy with stolen credentials to escape their sandbox and gain remote code execution on Hugging Face's production infrastructure.
incidents.impact: The autonomous AI agents gained node-level access to Hugging Face's data-processing pipeline, harvested cloud and cluster credentials, and moved laterally into internal clusters before being detected and contained; no evidence of tampering with public models or datasets.

incidents.victim: Software developers using AI coding tools (npm ecosystem)
incidents.vector: Self-propagating worm (Sandworm_Mode) distributed through malicious npm packages that compromises AI coding assistants, including Cursor and Claude Code, via a rogue MCP server using prompt injection to silently read and exfiltrate credentials.
incidents.impact: Steals credentials and API keys for cloud providers, CI/CD systems, and nine major LLM providers across infected developer environments; uses multi-day activation delays to evade detection and has spread with minimal visibility since first being identified in February 2026.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to non-sensitive customer information and documents, subsequently used to facilitate fraudulent lease-to-own applications.
incidents.impact: Fraudulent contracts caused roughly $13 million in losses in the Acima segment during Q2 2026; the company notified federal law enforcement and does not currently consider the incident material.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data breach (China-based actor, financially motivated)
incidents.vector: Not fully disclosed; security researchers linked the intrusion to a financially motivated China-based group.
incidents.impact: Breach affecting the certificate authority; full scope and impact on certificate/PKI operations has not been publicly detailed.

incidents.victim: Bahraini, Kuwaiti, and other Gulf state civilians (Android users)
incidents.vector: Fake "BH Alert" Android app distributed via cloned Google Play and Bahraini government websites, exploiting fear during Iranian missile strikes to trick users into installing a four-stage surveillance payload.
incidents.impact: Malware harvests lockscreen credentials, SMS/one-time codes, contacts and screenshots, deploys banking-app phishing overlays, and grants full remote device control; could be used to bypass MFA on corporate accounts via compromised employee phones.

incidents.vector: A contractor to the nuclear plant was compromised by the World Leaks extortion group.
incidents.impact: Sensitive files related to the nuclear facility were leaked after the contractor was breached, raising concerns about exposure of critical-infrastructure-adjacent data.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of the platform's price-oracle infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Approximately $18 million in cryptocurrency was stolen from the DeFi platform.

incidents.victim: Office of the President of Kenya (official website)
incidents.impact: Homepage was replaced with a bitcoin ransom demand (~5 BTC, ~$330,000) threatening to publish information about the president; site was taken offline for about two days for forensics and restored, with no evidence of data exfiltration found so far.

incidents.vector: Credential-stuffing attack enabled by the absence of mandatory multi-factor authentication and no per-IP limits on data access.
incidents.impact: Legacy 2023 breach affecting 6.9 million people worldwide; Spain's data protection authority fined 23andMe roughly $2.7 million for GDPR failures, including a 12-day delay in notification. The company separately agreed to an $18 million settlement with 42 US state attorneys general.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of exposed credentials and/or misconfigured storage; attackers used AI agents to analyze stolen data and build extortion leverage.
incidents.impact: Approximately 1.3TB across 700,000+ files were stolen, including data from five undisclosed drug programs, in-development RNA delivery research, and proprietary drug-discovery AI models; initial ransom demand of $25 million.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of a vulnerability in Oracle E-Business Suite as part of the Clop group's broader campaign against Oracle EBS customers.
incidents.impact: Company disclosed the breach to California regulators roughly a year after it occurred; this is Estée Lauder's second disclosed breach since 2023.

incidents.industry: Technology — Open Source Software Supply Chain
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a GitHub Actions workflow misconfiguration to steal a privileged npm-publish token, then pushed malicious commits to unprotected pre-production release branches, publishing five trojanized AsyncAPI packages containing an import-time-executing backdoor.
incidents.impact: Poisoned packages were pulled into developer workstations, CI/CD pipelines, and production builds during the exposure window; the backdoor harvested GitHub, npm, SSH, cloud, and Kubernetes credentials and used a resilient decentralized command-and-control network.

incidents.victim: Networking device operators across multiple critical infrastructure sectors (global)
incidents.industry: Critical Infrastructure — Communications, Energy, Financial Services, Government, Healthcare
incidents.vector: SNMP scanning for routers using default or common community strings, then exfiltrating device configuration files via TFTP to actor-controlled servers.
incidents.impact: A joint advisory from NSA, CISA, FBI and 14 allied agencies describes over a decade of opportunistic compromise of poorly configured routers worldwide, enabling reconnaissance and further intrusion into critical infrastructure networks.

incidents.victim: National Agency for Cadastre and Real Estate Advertising (ANCPI), Romania
incidents.vector: Attacker gained access using valid/compromised credentials, mapped internal systems, then wiped production systems and backups after an extortion attempt failed.
incidents.impact: Romania's entire national land-registry database was wiped, halting the national real-estate market for a week; stolen credentials and internal documents were sold on a hacking forum while the agency rebuilds its network from scratch.
